title: Missing Key in Dict Raises KeyError

bugs.explanation: Accessing a missing key with `dict[key]` raises `KeyError`. Use `dict.get(key, default)` to return a fallback value when the key is absent, avoiding the exception.

title: Iterating dict Gives Keys Not Items

bugs.explanation: Iterating a dict directly yields keys (strings). `item[0]` and `item[1]` would then index the key string by character, not give the key-value pair. Use `scores.items()` to iterate over `(key, value)` tuples.

`groups['team_a']` raises `KeyError` because the key doesn't exist yet. Use `setdefault('team_a', [])` which creates an empty list for missing keys and returns it so you can immediately call `.append()`.

A `dict` and a `list` are different types and will never be equal. If the intent is to check whether the dict has exactly the key `'x'`, compare `list(data.keys()) == ['x']` or use `'x' in data and len(data) == 1`.

title: Mutable Default Argument in Dict

bugs.explanation: The default mutable dict `{}` is created once and shared across all calls. Each call without an explicit `store` will keep accumulating values from previous calls. Use `None` as the default and initialise inside: `if store is None: store = {}`.
`{}` creates an empty **dict**, not an empty **set**. The output would be `<class 'dict'>`. To create an empty set, use the `set()` constructor.

title: Set Intersection Operator

bugs.explanation: Duplicate keys in a dict literal are allowed by Python but the last value silently wins — `'name'` becomes `'Bob'`. This is almost always a bug. If you need a second name-like field, use a different key such as `'nickname'`.
Lists are mutable and therefore unhashable — they cannot be used as dict keys. Use a tuple instead: `(1, 2, 3)`. Tuples are immutable and hashable.

title: Counting Items With a Dict

bugs.explanation: `set.remove(elem)` raises `KeyError` if the element is not present. If you want to safely remove an element that may or may not be in the set, use `set.discard(elem)` which does nothing when the element is absent.

title: Dict Comprehension
code:
squares = {x: x**2 for x in range(1, 6)}
print(squares)

title: in Checks Keys Not Values in Dict

bugs.explanation: `in` on a dict checks keys, not values. `'Alice' in d` checks whether `'Alice'` is a key, not whether it is a value. To check values, use `'Alice' in d.values()`.

title: Symmetric Difference of Sets

bugs.explanation: `config['db']['port']` raises `KeyError` because `'port'` does not exist in the nested dict. Use `.get()` with a default: `config['db'].get('port', 5432)`.
